newsitem.title: USA: Kerr-McGee to review payout increase.
newsitem.headline: Kerr-McGee to review payout increase.

text.p: Kerr-McGee Corp financial performance has put the question of a dividend increase on the table and the board is expected to review the issue early next year, President Luke R. Corbett told analysts on Tuesday.
The company is now paying $0.41 per share quarterly.
It reported third quarter net income from continuing operations of $1.17 per share, up 105 percent from 1995.

"Our strong financial performance certainly puts the question of a dividend increase on the table. We are putting together the relevant information so that our board can review that issue early next year," Corbett told the analysts.

In the statement releasing his comments, Kerr-McGee said it expects to produce 43 million barrels of oil equivalent in 1996 while adding about 69 million barrels to its reserve base, a 160 percent production replacement.
It said these reserves were added at finding and development costs averaging $4.20 per barrel.
The company said oil production in 1996 and 1997 is projected to essentially equal the 1995 record of 70,000 barrels per day, even considering recent divestitures of 4,000 barrels daily.
Production is projected to grow to 80,000 barrels daily in 1998.
In 1997 and thereafter, the statement noted, Kerr-McGee's production figures include its share of Devon Energy Corp's production.
Kerr-McGee expects to own 31 percent of Devon after merging its North American onshore production with the company in a transaction scheduled to become effective January 1.
It said natural gas production volumes will approximate 300 million cubic feet per day, about the same as in 1995, after divestitures of 40 million cubic feet daily since 1995.
The divestiture of the company's nonstrategic properties will be completed in 1996.
During the year, it expects to sell 23 million barrels of oil equivalent reserves. Proceeds are projected at about $90 million, Kerr-McGee said.

It said work is under way on the plan of development for the North Sea's Janice field, where a Kerr-McGee appraisal well tested at a combined rate of 33,000 barrels of oil per day from several Jurassic zones. Kerr-McGee operates this block with a 50.9 percent interest.
The company noted it has a 33 percent interest in Indonesia's North Geragai field where production is scheduled to start in the third quarter of 1997.

North Geragai production will start at about 4,000 barrels of liquids per day and should increase to 10,000 barrels per day in 1998. Reserves are estimated at 32 million barrels of oil and 170 billion cubic feet of natural gas.
Kerr-McGee said it projects an annual demand growth rate of 3 to 4 percent for its most important chemical product, titanium dioxide pigment.
Sales of the company's manganese dioxide, a key ingredient in alkaline dry-cell batteries, are expected to grow by 5 to 8 percent through the year 2000.
Kerr-McGee is working with customers to develop new rechargeable and throw-away batteries, which could further increase sales.

Annual market growth for Kerr-McGee's sodium chlorate, used in pulp and paper bleaching, is expected to reach 6 to 8 percent through the year 2000. Capacity is being expanded from the present 120,000 tons per year to 143,000 tons by 1998.
Kerr-McGee noted demand for utility-grade, low-sulfur coal is continuing to increase due to Clean Air Act requirements.

In response to this increase in demand, capacity at the company's Jacobs Ranch surface mine in northeastern Wyoming is being increased to 39 million tons from 24 million tons annually, the company said.
Shipments from Kerr-McGee's underground Galatia Mine in Illinois should reach a record 6.6 million tons in 1996.
Galatia is one of just a few mines in the Midwest that produce lower-sulfur coal, which can be burned by utilities during Phase I of the Clean Air Act without using scrubbers or emission allowances.
-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
